app/server.mjs:88 — ability route plus its imports at app/server.mjs:6,14 must be removed separately from the view
app/src/views.mjs:591 — the Pokémon page's Abilities section links to /abilities, so dropping the pages means editing an unrelated page
app/src/views.mjs:602 — dead renderAbilityPageByName is a second copy a remover must also find
app/src/api.mjs:169 — getAbility becomes dead after route removal
removability.rationale: Removing Abilities is a grep-able but scattered handful of edits across four files (~7 sites), including a dead duplicate and a section on the Pokémon page; no feature-module boundary exists to delete.

evidence: app/src/render.mjs:66 — pokemonCard is the single card component, so the Deoxys-style sprite fix in spriteUrl (app/src/api.mjs:46) covers every list
app/src/views.mjs:153 — type-page list assembly, sorting by id
app/src/views.mjs:226 — move-page list assembly, a near-copy with a different fallback
app/src/views.mjs:254 — ability-page list assembly re-implements the dedupe/sort with a hidden flag instead of reusing dedupeSortedPokemonEntries
app/src/views.mjs:596 — unused renderMovePageByName duplicates the 404 flow that app/server.mjs:81-96 implements inline
changeability.rationale: Rendering bugs in shared components land in one place, but list-assembly/ordering logic is duplicated across four sites and the fetch-or-404 flow exists twice (one copy dead), so several realistic fixes need N coordinated edits.

evidence: app/src/api.mjs — single data module; base URL and API_ROOT are private (lines 1-2), nothing outside knows them
app/server.mjs:58 — htmx target id 'pokemon-results' compared as a string literal, duplicating the id in app/src/render.mjs:103 markup
app/server.mjs:124 — same pattern for 'moves', duplicating app/src/views.mjs:460; renaming a target needs coordinated edits
app/src/views.mjs:1 — imports 21 symbols from api.mjs and reaches into raw API payload shapes (e.g. species.varieties at views.mjs:538)
app/src/views.mjs:37 and app/src/views.mjs:534 — page-data assembly lives in views.mjs for home/pokemon but inline in app/server.mjs:81-96 for move/ability/type, so the same concern has two homes
coupling.rationale: Server, views and data are honestly layered with no shared mutable state, but the htmx target-id contract is a string duplicated across files, views.mjs has a wide 21-symbol import surface into raw API shapes, and page-data assembly is inconsistently placed.

evidence: app/src/render.mjs:66-83 — cardGrid/pokemonCard genuinely stretch across four pages and the hidden-ability variant via props
app/src/render.mjs:85-92 — section() helper used by five sections, but its sectionId flag parameter (line 87) is never used by any caller
app/src/views.mjs:459 — renderMovesSection bypasses section() and inlines the whole section chrome, so the section contract is defined twice
app/src/api.mjs:85-99 — memoize is a well-fitted abstraction for the three catalogs
app/src/views.mjs:261 — ability list re-implements type/move list assembly rather than parameterizing one helper
abstraction_design.rationale: The shared primitives (cards, sections, badges, layout, memoized catalogs) stretch well, but the abstraction breaks exactly where the real variation is: one list pipeline is copy-pasted three ways and the moves section falls outside the section() abstraction, leaving a dead flag parameter behind.

findings.issue: renderMovePageByName / renderAbilityPageByName / renderTypePageByName are exported but never imported; they duplicate the fetch-or-404 flow that server.mjs:81-96 implements inline, so a behavior fix has two homes and one is silently dead.
findings.suggestion: Delete all three, or move them into server.mjs as the single 'load or 404' path so there is exactly one copy.

findings.issue: The 'API entries → Pokémon cards' pipeline (exclude forms >10000, dedupe by id, map id→species, sort by dex) is implemented three times: type page (:153), move page (:226) and ability page (:254-268), each slightly different, so ordering/limit changes must be made N times.
findings.suggestion: Extract one entriesToCards(entries, { speciesCatalog, decorate }) helper in render.mjs and have all three pages (plus any future Items page) call it.

findings.issue: All HTML is raw template literals with a hand-rolled escapeHtml; with ~100 interpolation sites, zero type checking and zero comments across 1,557 lines, every new interpolation is an unescaped-output bug waiting to happen.
findings.suggestion: Use hono/html's html tagged template (or hono/jsx) for automatic escaping, and add JSDoc types to the public helpers at minimum.

findings.issue: renderMovesSection inlines the <section class="panel" aria-labelledby=…> chrome instead of using the section() helper, because section() can't express an element id — so the section contract is defined twice and the sectionId parameter that would fix it (render.mjs:87) is dead.
findings.suggestion: Use section({ id: 'moves', sectionId: 'moves', ... }) or restructure section() to take one id used for both the element and the heading, then route the moves section through it.

findings.issue: Static assets are served via three bespoke routes that read files into memory at startup, instead of serveStatic from @hono/node-server/serve-static; adding any new static file means editing server.mjs and a new route.
findings.suggestion: Replace the three routes with app.use('*', serveStatic({ root: fileURLToPath(new URL('./public', import.meta.url)) })) per the current Node.js adapter docs.

findings.issue: htmx target ids ('pokemon-results' at :58, 'moves' at :124) are string literals duplicated in the markup (render.mjs:103, views.mjs:460); renaming a target requires coordinated edits that nothing will catch if missed.
findings.suggestion: Export shared constants for target ids from render.mjs and use them in both the markup and the HX-Target checks.

findings.issue: Three separate caching mechanisms (response cache/pending at :5-6 and :40-72, memoize at :85-99, versionGroupCache at :180-185) are all unbounded Maps with no invalidation; changing caching rules means reconciling three mechanisms in one file.
findings.suggestion: Route version-group fetches through the shared fetchJson/apiGet cache and drop versionGroupCache, so cache policy lives in exactly one place.

findings.issue: Page-data assembly is inconsistently placed: getHomeData/getPokemonPageData live in views.mjs (:37, :534) while the equivalent for move/ability/type pages is inlined in the route handlers, so the 'page data' pattern must be discovered twice.
findings.suggestion: Pick one convention — either a data function per page next to its render function, or all data assembly in server.mjs — and apply it uniformly.

findings.issue: The move-table htmx partial endpoint calls the full getPokemonPageData (species + default pokemon + evolution chain + species catalog + all move details for the game) just to render one table, coupling a lightweight partial to heavyweight page assembly.
findings.suggestion: Give the endpoint a narrow data path (species lookup + moves for the selected game) rather than reusing the whole page-data function.

findings.issue: Minor dead exports and an unused flag: PAGE_SIZE is exported but never imported, and section()'s sectionId parameter (render.mjs:87) has no callers.
findings.suggestion: Remove the export and the unused parameter; dead knobs mislead future maintainers about intended usage.

summary: The app is honestly layered — a single data module, a small shared-render kit, thin routes — and its shared components are good enough that the hardest real bug (the Deoxys sprite) would land in one place. But there is no per-feature boundary: everything lives in a 623-line views file where list assembly is copy-pasted three ways, the fetch-or-404 flow exists twice (one copy dead), and markup is hand-escaped template strings with no types or comments. It is comfortably acceptable and easy to grep, but every scenario requires finding duplicated sites by reading rather than by structure.
